L01 | What remains judgment is whether the comparison was truly against something outside yourself and sufficient to mark the answer checked.
L02 | What remains judgment is whether another source could change the answer you owe and when the search you reported is enough to stop.
L03 | What remains judgment is which lesson must become an always-done step and whether this moment is the case that step was written for.
L04 | What remains judgment is what counts as having actually landed and whether the gap from the success report is serious enough to reject it.
L05 | What remains judgment is whether a wrong location or a bad reading has been excluded well enough to say the thing is truly lost.
L06 | What remains judgment is which clock is authoritative and which moment the written time is supposed to record.
L07 | What remains judgment is what test would actually stress the noted fact and whether a warning the note dropped changes what you may repeat.
L08 | What remains judgment is which cause is the real one once the words have been quoted and the name-shaped guess has been set aside.
L09 | What remains judgment is which failure to provoke and whether one deliberate failure is enough to trust this test or monitor for this use.
L10 | What remains judgment is whether calm attention is what was asked and what, in this moment, would count as something else.
L11 | What remains judgment is which work is important enough and what difference in a reviewer would actually catch this kind of error.
L12 | What remains judgment is how far the search must be pressed before an empty result, a zero, or a short list can be treated as a fact about the world.
L13 | What remains judgment is how much evidence is actually in hand and whether that amount supports the claim you are about to make.
L14 | What remains judgment is what observable action would show the saved change is truly in effect and when its absence has been seen long enough.
L15 | What remains judgment is which things sit close enough beside the fix that they must be checked and how far that neighborhood extends.
L16 | What remains judgment is which check is the one deciding check for this work and whether passing it is enough to say done or verified.
L17 | What remains judgment is whether the string is a long code or hash that must not be copied by hand and whether the program copied the intended span.
